metadata.title: Multiplicity of continuous maps between manifolds

nodes.name: Lower bound on the multiplicity of a continuous map
nodes.statement: We consider a continuous map $f :M\to N$ between two manifolds and try to estimate its multiplicity from below, i.e. find a $q$-tuple of pairwise distinct points $x_1,\ldots, x_q\in M$ such that $f(x_1) = f(x_2) = \ldots = f(x_q)$.
nodes.section: Abstract
nodes.statement_short: Estimate from below the multiplicity of a continuous map $f:M\to N$, i.e. find a coincident $q$-tuple.

nodes.name: Multiple points
nodes.statement: In this paper we consider a continuous map $f :M\to N$ between two manifolds and try to find some sufficient conditions for existence of \emph{multiple points}, i.e. the $q$-tuples of pairwise distinct point $x_1,\ldots, x_q\in M$ such that $$ f(x_1) = f(x_2) = \ldots = f(x_q). $$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Multiple points of $f$ are $q$-tuples of pairwise distinct points of $M$ with a common image.
nodes.genus: $q$-tuples of pairwise distinct point $x_1,\ldots, x_q\in M$

nodes.name: Coincident $q$-tuple and multiplicity
nodes.statement: We call such a $q$-tuple $x_1,\ldots, x_q$ a \emph{coincident $q$-tuple}, and call the \emph{multiplicity} of $f$ the maximum $q$ such that there exists a coincident $q$-tuple for $f$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: The multiplicity of $f$ is the largest $q$ admitting a coincident $q$-tuple.

nodes.name: Canonical form of $\Sigma^{1^k}$ singularities
nodes.statement: Let the local coordinates be $(x_1,\ldots, x_m)$ in $M$ and $(y_1,\ldots, y_n)$ in $N$. Then the map is given by \begin{eqnarray} y_i &=& x_i,\ i=1,\ldots, m-1\\ y_i &=& \sum_{l=1}^k x_{(i-m)k + l} x_m^l,\ i=m,\ldots, n-1\\ y_n &=& \sum_{l=1}^{k-1} x_{(n-m)k + l} x_m^l + x_m^{k+1}, \end{eqnarray}
nodes.section: 2 Local multiplicity of generic smooth maps -- the approach of singularity theory
nodes.statement_short: Morin's local normal form for a generic smooth map with a $\Sigma^{1^k}$ singularity.

nodes.name: Codimension condition for the canonical form
nodes.statement: here the inequality $k(n-m+1)\le m$ must hold.

nodes.name: Coincident $(k+1)$-tuple from the canonical form
nodes.statement: If we select the numbers $x_i$ ($i=1,\ldots m-1$) so that the polynomials in $x_m$ in the right part of (\ref{pol-mid}) are zero, and the right part of (\ref{pol-last}) has $k+1$ distinct roots, then we obtain a coincident $(k+1)$-tuple, since the coordinate $x_m$ has $k+1$ possible choices.

nodes.statement_short: Choosing the parameters so the leading polynomial has $k+1$ roots produces a coincident $(k+1)$-tuple.

the right part of (\ref{pol-last}) has $k+1$ distinct roots

nodes.statement: The classes $\sigma_{k, m-n}$ for singularities of type $\Sigma^{1^k}$ in codimension $m-n$ can be expressed in terms of Stiefel-Whitney classes by some recurrent formulas, see~\cite{port1971} for example.

nodes.statement_short: The singularity classes are recursively expressible in Stiefel-Whitney classes.

nodes.name: Configuration space $K^q(X)$
nodes.statement: For a topological space $X$ denote the \emph{configuration space} $$ K^q(X) = \{(x_1, \ldots, x_q)\in X^q : \forall i,j\ x_i\not= x_j\}. $$
nodes.section: 3 Global multiplicity and configuration spaces

nodes.name: Free $\Sg_q$-action on $K^q(X)$
nodes.statement: Note that the permutation group $\Sg_q$ acts freely on $K^q(X)$.
nodes.section: 3 Global multiplicity and configuration spaces
assumptions: For a topological space $X$
conclusions: the permutation group $\Sg_q$ acts freely on $K^q(X)$

nodes.name: Restricted power map $f^q$
nodes.statement: For any continuous map $f: M\to N$ denote its power $f^q : K^q(M)\to N^q$ its power restricted to $K^q(M)$. This is an $\Sg_q$-equivariant map.
nodes.section: 3 Global multiplicity and configuration spaces

nodes.name: Coincident $q$-tuples as diagonal intersection
nodes.statement: A coincident $q$-tuple is an intersection of $f^q(K^q(X))$ with the (thin) diagonal $\Delta(N)\subseteq N^q$.
nodes.section: 3 Global multiplicity and configuration spaces
nodes.statement_short: Coincident tuples are exactly where the power map meets the thin diagonal.
assumptions: For any continuous map $f: M\to N$
conclusions: A coincident $q$-tuple is an intersection of $f^q(K^q(X))$ with the (thin) diagonal $\Delta(N)\subseteq N^q$

nodes.name: Preimage of the diagonal as an obstruction
nodes.statement: Thus the preimage of the diagonal $(f^q)^{-1}(\Delta(N))\subseteq K^q(M)$ can be considered as an obstruction to deforming the map $f$ so that it has no coincident $q$-tuples.
nodes.section: 3 Global multiplicity and configuration spaces
nodes.statement_short: The diagonal preimage obstructs deforming $f$ to a map without coincident $q$-tuples.
conclusions: the preimage of the diagonal $(f^q)^{-1}(\Delta(N))\subseteq K^q(M)$ can be considered as an obstruction to deforming the map $f$ so that it has no coincident $q$-tuples

nodes.name: Obstruction class $s_q(f)$
nodes.statement: In the case when $M$ and $N$ are smooth manifolds of dimensions $m$ and $n$ respectively, and $M$ is compact, this preimage of the diagonal can be considered as an $\Sg_q$-equivariant cohomology class $$ s_q(f)\in H_{\Sg_q}^{n(q-1)}(K^q(M)) = H^{n(q-1)}(K^q(M)/{\Sg_q}), $$ the coefficients of the cohomology being $Z_2$, or $\mathbb Z$, possibly with the sign action of the group $\Sg_q$ depending on the orientability of $N$ and parity of its dimension.
nodes.section: 3 Global multiplicity and configuration spaces
nodes.statement_short: For compact smooth $M$ the diagonal preimage defines an $\Sg_q$-equivariant class $s_q(f)$ of degree $n(q-1)$.

nodes.name: Cobordism interpretation of the obstruction
nodes.statement: Certainly, this obstruction can also be considered as an oriented or non-oriented cobordism class in $\Omega_{(S)O}^{n(q-1)}(K^q(M)/{\Sg_q})$, but we do not use the cobordism in this paper.
nodes.section: 3 Global multiplicity and configuration spaces

nodes.name: Relation of the global class to local double points
nodes.statement: The global cohomology class for double points has certain relation with the local double points in the case $N=\mathbb R^n$, see~\cite{wu1958,schw1966,mcc1978} for example. For multiplicity $>2$ we restrict ourselves to studying the local (in some sense) multiplicity in the following sections.
nodes.section: 3 Global multiplicity and configuration spaces
nodes.statement_short: For $q=2$ the global class relates to local double points; higher $q$ is treated locally here.

nodes.name: Local multiple points
nodes.statement: This approach would give multiple points, that are close enough to each other in $M$. We call such multiple points \emph{local}.
nodes.section: 4 Local multiplicity of continuous maps -- the configuration space bundle
differentia: that are close enough to each other in $M$

nodes.name: Local multiplicity here is stronger than in the smooth generic case
nodes.statement: Note that this type of local multiplicity is stronger than the local multiplicity in the smooth generic case (see Section~\ref{generic-smooth}), because here we may guarantee the existence of a coincident $q$-tuple $\{x_1,\ldots, x_q\}$ with some small but bounded from below diameter, the bound depending on $M$ only. In will be clear from the definition of $Q^q(M,\ldots)$ in Section~\ref{coind-char}.
nodes.section: 4 Local multiplicity of continuous maps -- the configuration space bundle
nodes.statement_short: The coincident tuple obtained has diameter bounded below by a constant depending only on $M$.

nodes.name: Configuration space bundle $K_M^q(\xi)$
nodes.statement: Let $\xi : E(\xi)\to M$ be a vector or disc bundle over $M$. The subspace of $K^q(E(\xi))$, consisting of configurations lying in the same fiber of $\xi$, is denoted $K_M^q(\xi)$ and called the \emph{configuration space bundle}.
nodes.section: 4 Local multiplicity of continuous maps -- the configuration space bundle
differentia: consisting of configurations lying in the same fiber of $\xi$

nodes.name: Fiberwise map $\phi = \exp_N^{-1}\circ f^2\circ \exp_M$
nodes.statement: Now let us consider a continuous map $f :M\to N$. Let us take small enough tangent disc bundle $DN$ so that $\exp$ (of $N$) is invertible on it. Then take small enough tangent disc bundle $DM$ so that the inclusion for the map of pairs $f^2\circ\exp_M DM\subset \exp_N DN$ holds. Then a fiberwise map $$ \phi = \exp_N^{-1}\circ f^2\circ \exp_M : DM\to DN $$ is defined.
nodes.section: 4 Local multiplicity of continuous maps -- the configuration space bundle
nodes.statement_short: Exponential charts on $M$ and $N$ turn $f$ into a fiberwise map $\phi : DM\to DN$ of disc bundles.

nodes.name: Reduction of local multiplicity to the fiberwise map $\psi : DM \to f^*(DN)$
nodes.statement: So the local multiplicity is bounded from below if we bound from below a multiplicity in the fiberwise map $$ \psi : DM \to f^*(DN) $$ over the same space $M$.
nodes.section: 4 Local multiplicity of continuous maps -- the configuration space bundle
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to bound the multiplicity of the fiberwise map $\psi : DM \to f^*(DN)$ over $M$.
assumptions: if we bound from below a multiplicity in the fiberwise map $$ \psi : DM \to f^*(DN) $$ over the same space $M$
conclusions: the local multiplicity is bounded from below

nodes.name: Representation $A_q$
nodes.statement: Let $A_q$ be the $q-1$-dimensional representation of $\Sg_q$, arising from the natural permutation representation on $\mathbb R^q$ by taking the quotient $\mathbb R^q/(1,1,\ldots,1)$.
nodes.section: 4 Local multiplicity of continuous maps -- the configuration space bundle
differentia: arising from the natural permutation representation on $\mathbb R^q$ by taking the quotient $\mathbb R^q/(1,1,\ldots,1)$

nodes.name: Coincident $q$-tuples as the zero set of the section $\psi_0^q$
nodes.statement: Now the coincident $q$-tuples correspond to the zero set of the section $\psi_0^q$, and we have reduced the problem of finding local multiple points to proving that the zero set of the $\Sg_q$-equivariant vector bundle $A_q\otimes(\xi^q)^*(\eta)$ over $K_M^q(\xi)$ is nonempty.
nodes.section: 4 Local multiplicity of continuous maps -- the configuration space bundle
nodes.statement_short: Finding local multiple points becomes showing an equivariant bundle section has a zero.
conclusions: the coincident $q$-tuples correspond to the zero set of the section $\psi_0^q$

nodes.name: Zero set $Z(\psi^q, \xi, \eta)$
nodes.statement: Now let us consider the zero set $Z(\psi^q, \xi, \eta)$ of some $\Sg_q$-equivariant section of the bundle $A_q\otimes(\xi^q)^*(\eta)$ over $K_M^q(\xi)$. We shall denote the bundle simply $A_q\otimes \eta$ since it does not lead to a confusion.
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
differentia: of some $\Sg_q$-equivariant section of the bundle $A_q\otimes(\xi^q)^*(\eta)$ over $K_M^q(\xi)$

nodes.name: Poincare duality of the coincidence set to the Euler class
nodes.statement: Certainly, the set $Z(\psi^q, \xi, \eta)$ may be considered a manifold for generic sections, and it is Poincare dual to the Euler class $e(A_q\otimes \eta)$, taken in the equivariatn cohomology or some bordism theory.
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
nodes.statement_short: For generic sections the coincidence set is Poincare dual to $e(A_q\otimes\eta)$.
conclusions: the set $Z(\psi^q, \xi, \eta)$ may be considered a manifold for generic sections, and it is Poincare dual to the Euler class $e(A_q\otimes \eta)$, taken in the equivariatn cohomology or some bordism theory

nodes.name: Stabilization identity for the coincidence set
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} Z((\psi\oplus\iota)^q, \xi\oplus\zeta, \eta\oplus\zeta) = Z(\psi^q, \xi, \eta)\times_M \zeta. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
nodes.statement_short: Adding an identity summand $\zeta$ multiplies the coincidence set by $\zeta$.

nodes.name: Nonzero stabilized Euler class forces a nonempty coincidence set
nodes.statement: Hence if the Euler class $e(A_q\otimes(\eta\oplus\zeta))$ is nonzero over $K_M^q(\xi\oplus\zeta)$, then the set $Z(\psi^q, \xi, \eta)$ cannot be empty.
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
assumptions: if the Euler class $e(A_q\otimes(\eta\oplus\zeta))$ is nonzero over $K_M^q(\xi\oplus\zeta)$
conclusions: the set $Z(\psi^q, \xi, \eta)$ cannot be empty

nodes.name: Trivialization reduction lemma
nodes.statement: The coincident $q$-tuples in a continuous fiberwise map $\psi : \xi\to\eta$ over $M$ are guaranteed by a nonzero $\Sg_q$-equivariant Euler class $e(A_q\otimes(\xi^\perp\oplus\eta))$ in the cohomology (or cobordism) of $K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)\times M$, where $\mu=\dim \xi + \dim \xi^\perp$.
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
nodes.statement_short: A nonzero equivariant Euler class over $K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)\times M$ guarantees coincident $q$-tuples.
assumptions: a continuous fiberwise map $\psi : \xi\to\eta$ over $M$
a nonzero $\Sg_q$-equivariant Euler class $e(A_q\otimes(\xi^\perp\oplus\eta))$ in the cohomology (or cobordism) of $K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)\times M$
$\mu=\dim \xi + \dim \xi^\perp$
conclusions: The coincident $q$-tuples in a continuous fiberwise map $\psi : \xi\to\eta$ over $M$ are guaranteed

nodes.name: Proof of the trivialization reduction lemma
nodes.statement: In the above reasoning take $\zeta$ to be $\xi^\perp$ such that $\xi\oplus\xi^\perp = \epsilon^\mu$, $\epsilon$ denotes a trivial vector bundle. Then it suffices to note that $$ K_M^q(\epsilon^\mu) = K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)\times M. $$
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
nodes.statement_short: Stabilize by the normal complement $\xi^\perp$ so the configuration space bundle trivializes.

nodes.name: Stabilize by $\xi^\perp$
nodes.statement: In the above reasoning take $\zeta$ to be $\xi^\perp$ such that $\xi\oplus\xi^\perp = \epsilon^\mu$, $\epsilon$ denotes a trivial vector bundle.
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
nodes.statement_short: Choose the stabilizing bundle to be a normal complement making $\xi\oplus\xi^\perp$ trivial.

nodes.name: Trivialized configuration space bundle splits
nodes.statement: Then it suffices to note that $$ K_M^q(\epsilon^\mu) = K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)\times M. $$
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
nodes.statement_short: Conclude from the product decomposition of the configuration space bundle of a trivial bundle.

nodes.name: K\"unneth splitting of $H_{\Sg_q}^*(K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)\times M)$
nodes.statement: If we consider the cohomology with coefficients in a field $Z_p$, then by the K\"unneth formula the algebra $H_{\Sg_q}^*(K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)\times M)$ is a free $H^*(M)$-module, spanned by the linear basis of $H^*(K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)/{\Sg_q})$.
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
nodes.statement_short: Over a field the equivariant cohomology is a free $H^*(M)$-module.
assumptions: If we consider the cohomology with coefficients in a field $Z_p$
conclusions: the algebra $H_{\Sg_q}^*(K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)\times M)$ is a free $H^*(M)$-module, spanned by the linear basis of $H^*(K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)/{\Sg_q})$

nodes.name: Basis $h_i$ can be taken inside $H^*(B\Sg_q, Z_2)$
nodes.statement: Denote the latter basis by $(h_1,\ldots, h_{N(q,\mu)})$, it is known (see~\cite{fuks1970,vass1994,rot2008}) that in the case $p=2$ the elements $h_i$ can be selected to be part of the basis of $H^*(B\Sg_q, Z_2)$.
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
assumptions: in the case $p=2$
conclusions: the elements $h_i$ can be selected to be part of the basis of $H^*(B\Sg_q, Z_2)$

nodes.name: The classes $s_i$ depend only on characteristic classes of $\eta-\xi$
nodes.statement: Now we can decompose the Euler class $$ e(A_q\otimes (\xi^\perp\oplus\eta)) = \sum_{i=1}^{N(q,\mu)} s_ih_i $$ and obtain the elements $s_i\in H^*(M, Z_p)$, that depend naturally on the bundle $\xi^\perp\oplus\eta$. Hence $s_i$ only depend on the Stiefel-Whitney (in case $p=2$) or the Pontryagin and Euler (in case $p$ odd) classes of the virtual bundle $\eta-\xi$, since it is sufficient to consider the situation over some Grassmann variety and then use the naturality of construction.
nodes.section: 5 The Euler class of local multiple points
nodes.statement_short: Expanding the Euler class in the basis yields classes $s_i$ natural in the virtual bundle $\eta-\xi$.
conclusions: $s_i$ only depend on the Stiefel-Whitney (in case $p=2$) or the Pontryagin and Euler (in case $p$ odd) classes of the virtual bundle $\eta-\xi$

nodes.name: Top cohomology of $K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)/\Sg_q$ for prime powers
nodes.statement: In this case the cohomology $H^*(K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)/{\Sg_q}, A)$ is zero in dimensions $>(q-1)(\mu-1)$, and its $(q-1)(\mu-1)$-dimensional cohomology is generated by the class $e(A_q)^{n-1}$, see~\cite{vass1988,ossa1996,rot2008,kar2009} for different cases of these results. Here the coefficients $A$ are $Z_p$ for $p=2$ or odd $\mu$, and $Z_p$ with sign action of $\Sg_q$ in other cases.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: For $q$ a prime power the quotient configuration space has top cohomology generated by $e(A_q)^{n-1}$.
assumptions: Let us consider the case when $q$ is a power of a prime $p$.
conclusions: the cohomology $H^*(K^q(\mathbb R^\mu)/{\Sg_q}, A)$ is zero in dimensions $>(q-1)(\mu-1)$
its $(q-1)(\mu-1)$-dimensional cohomology is generated by the class $e(A_q)^{n-1}$

nodes.name: Leading term $s_{q, d}$ of the Euler class expansion
nodes.statement: Thus similar to the above definition, we can put $$ e(A_q\otimes (\xi^\perp\oplus\eta)) = s_{q, d}(\xi^\perp\oplus\eta) e(A_q)^{\mu-1} +\ldots, $$ where $d=\dim\eta-\dim\xi = \dim(\xi^\perp\oplus\eta) - \mu$ and $\ldots$ denotes the terms with the dimension of the corresponding class in $H^*(M, Z_p)$ larger, then that of $s_{q, d}$. Note that the dimension of $s_{q, d}$ equals $(q-1)(d+1)$.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: Define $s_{q,d}$ as the coefficient of $e(A_q)^{\mu-1}$ in the expansion of the equivariant Euler class.

nodes.name: Leading characteristic class of local coincident $q$-tuples
nodes.statement: We call $s_{q, d}(\eta-\xi)$ the \emph{leading characteristic class} of local coincident $q$-tuples for prime powers $q$ at codimension $d$.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
differentia: of local coincident $q$-tuples for prime powers $q$ at codimension $d$

nodes.name: Leading class of coincident $2^k$-tuples
nodes.statement: Let $q$ be a power of two. Denote $w_i$ the Stiefel-Whitney classes of $\eta-\xi$. Then as a polynomial in the Stiefel-Whitney classes of $\eta-\xi$ $$ s_{q, d}(\eta-\xi) \equiv w_{d+1}^{q-1} \mod w_{d+2}, w_{d+3}, \ldots. $$
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: For $q=2^k$ the leading class equals $w_{d+1}^{q-1}$ modulo higher Stiefel-Whitney classes.
assumptions: Let $q$ be a power of two.
Denote $w_i$ the Stiefel-Whitney classes of $\eta-\xi$.
conclusions: $$ s_{q, d}(\eta-\xi) \equiv w_{d+1}^{q-1} \mod w_{d+2}, w_{d+3}, \ldots. $$

nodes.name: The configuration $Q_0^q(\mathbb R^n, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$
nodes.statement: Let $q=2^k$ and consider a sequence $\delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k$ of positive integers such that for any $l<k$ $$ \delta_l > \sum_{i=l+1}^k \delta_i. $$ Let $Q_0^1(\mathbb R^n)$ be the configuration, consisting of one point at the origin. Let by induction $Q_0^q(\mathbb R^n, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$ be the set of all $q$-point configurations, such that the first $q/2$ points form a configuration of $Q_0^{q/2}(\mathbb R^n, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_k)$, shifted by a vector $u$ of length $\delta_1$, and the other $q/2$ points form a configuration of $Q_0^{q/2}(\mathbb R^n, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_k)$, shifted by a vector $-u$.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: Inductive doubling construction: two copies of the half-size configuration shifted by $\pm u$ with $|u|=\delta_1$.
differentia: such that the first $q/2$ points form a configuration of $Q_0^{q/2}(\mathbb R^n, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_k)$, shifted by a vector $u$ of length $\delta_1$, and the other $q/2$ points form a configuration of $Q_0^{q/2}(\mathbb R^n, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_k)$, shifted by a vector $-u$

nodes.name: Distance-midpoint description of $Q_0^q(\mathbb R^n, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$
nodes.statement: A configuration in $Q_0^q(\mathbb R^n, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$ can also be described inductively as $x_1,\ldots, x_q\in\mathbb R^n$ such that all the distances $\dist(x_{2i-1}, x_{2i}) = 2\delta_k$ and the midpoints of $[x_{2i-1}, x_{2i}]$ form a configuration of $Q_0^{q/2}(\mathbb R^n, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_{k-1})$.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: Equivalent description: consecutive pairs at distance $2\delta_k$ whose midpoints form the half-size configuration.
differentia: the midpoints of $[x_{2i-1}, x_{2i}]$ form a configuration of $Q_0^{q/2}(\mathbb R^n, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_{k-1})$

nodes.name: $Q_0^q(\mathbb R^n)$ is a product of $q-1$ spheres
nodes.statement: Note that $Q_0^q(\mathbb R^n, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$ is always a product of $q-1$ spheres of dimension $n-1$, and we shall omit $\delta_i$ in the notation since it does not change the diffeomorphism type of $Q^q(\mathbb R^n)$.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: The model configuration space is diffeomorphic to a product of $q-1$ spheres $S^{n-1}$.
conclusions: $Q_0^q(\mathbb R^n, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$ is always a product of $q-1$ spheres of dimension $n-1$

nodes.name: Configuration subbundle $Q_M^q(\xi)$
nodes.statement: Then we can naturally define the space $Q_M^q(\xi)\subset K_M^q(\xi)$ for any vector bundle $\xi : E(\xi)\to M$ as a bundle of corresponding $Q_0^q(\xi^{-1}(x))$ for $x\in M$.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.genus: a bundle of corresponding $Q_0^q(\xi^{-1}(x))$ for $x\in M$

nodes.name: Extension of the midpoint description to Riemannian manifolds
nodes.statement: Note that the Definition~\ref{Qq-defn2} (distance and midpoint characterization) can be applied to any Riemannian manifold $M$, if we allow the last center point (configuration $Q_0^1$) be any $x\in M$. The distances should be chosen small enough in order for the midpoint to be unique.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: The distance-midpoint description transfers to Riemannian manifolds once distances are small.

nodes.name: The configuration space $Q^q(M, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold. Define $Q^q(M, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)\subset K^q(M)$ for $q=2^k$ inductively as follows. $Q^1(M) = M$. For $q\ge 2$ let $Q^q(M, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$ be the set of $q$-tuples $x_1,\ldots, x_q\in M$ such that all the distances $\dist(x_{2i-1}, x_{2i}) = 2\delta_k$ and the midpoints of $[x_{2i-1}, x_{2i}]$ form a configuration of $Q^{q/2}(M, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_{k-1})$.
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: Riemannian analogue of $Q_0^q$, defined inductively by pair distances and midpoints.
differentia: the midpoints of $[x_{2i-1}, x_{2i}]$ form a configuration of $Q^{q/2}(M, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_{k-1})$

nodes.name: Metric realization of $Q^q(M,\ldots)$ as $Q_M^q(TM)$
nodes.statement: Let the injectivity radius of $M$ be $r$ and for all $i=1,\ldots, k$ $$ 2\delta_i < r. $$ Then $Q^q(M, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$ is a fiber bundle (the bundle map is the last stage midpoint) over $M$, and is naturally homeomorphic to $Q_M^q(TM)$
nodes.section: 6 Local coincident $p^k$-tuples and their characteristic classes
nodes.statement_short: If $2\delta_i<r$ then $Q^q(M,\ldots)$ is a bundle over $M$ homeomorphic to $Q_M^q(TM)$.
assumptions: Let the injectivity radius of $M$ be $r$ and for all $i=1,\ldots, k$ $$ 2\delta_i < r. $$
conclusions: $Q^q(M, \delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$ is a fiber bundle (the bundle map is the last stage midpoint) over $M$
is naturally homeomorphic to $Q_M^q(TM)$

nodes.name: Proof of the metric realization lemma
nodes.statement: Let us prove by induction. For any configuration $(x_1,\ldots, x_q)\in Q^q(M,\delta_1, \ldots, \delta_k)$ the midpoints of pairs $[x_1, x_2], [x_2,x_3],\ldots,[x_{q-1}, x_q]$ form a configuration in $Q^{q/2}(M,\delta_1, \ldots, \delta_{k-1})$. nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Now we are ready to prove Theorem~\ref{2k-fold-leading} using the geometric definition of $s_{q,d}$. Let us find $s_{q,d}$ for a certain fiberwise map over the Grassmannian $M=G_{n, d+1}$ of linear $n$-subspaces in $\mathbb R^{n+d+1}$. Denote the canonical $n$-dimensional bundle $\gamma : E(\gamma)\to G_{n, d+1}$. Now consider the map $$ f :\mathbb R^{n+d+1}\to \mathbb R^{n+d} $$ given by $$ f(x_1, \ldots, x_{n+d+1}) = (x_1 - x_{n+d+1}^2, x_2 - x_{n+d+1}^3,\ldots, x_{n+d} - x_{n+d+1}^{n+d+1}). $$ Each fiber of $\gamma$ is mapped with this map to $\mathbb R^{n+d}$, so $f$ can be considered as a fiberwise map of $\gamma$ to $\epsilon^{n+d}$. Let us describe the coincident $q$-tuples of $f$ in $Q_M^q(\gamma)$. First, note that there is a natural inclusion $Q_M^q(\gamma)\to Q_0^q(\mathbb R^{n+d+1})$. A configuration of $q$ points $(p_1, \ldots, p_q)\in Q_0^q(\mathbb R^{n+d+1})$ is mapped to one point $y$ if they lie on a single curve $C(c_1, \ldots, c_{n+d})$, given by the parameterization $$ x_1 = c_1 + t^2,\ x_2 = c_2 + t^3,\ \ldots,\ x_{n+d} = c_{n+d} + t^{n+d+1},\ x_{n+d+1} = t. $$ Consider a single curve $C(c_1,\ldots,c_{n+m})$ and the set $Z(c_1,\ldots, c_{n+m})$ of all configurations in $Q^q(\mathbb R^n)$ (not $Q_0^q$!), lying entirely on $C(c_1,\ldots,c_{n+d})$. Consider a configuration $(p_1,\ldots, p_q)\in Z(c_1,\ldots, c_{n+m})$ and assume that the points are ordered w.r.t. the coordinate $x_{n+d+1}$, which corresponds with the parameter on the curve. From Definition~\ref{Qq-defn2} it is clear that if $\delta_i$ are small enough in the definition (so that the curvature of $C(c_1,\ldots, c_{n+m})$ becomes negligible), then the configuration $(p_1,\ldots, p_q)\in Z(c_1,\ldots, c_{n+m})$ is determined uniquely by any one point $p_i$, which can be chosen arbitrarily. In other words, $p_i$ is a smooth parameter on $Z(c_1, \ldots, c_{n+m})/\Sy_q$. Denote $$ Z=\bigcup_{c_1,\ldots,c_{n+d}\in\mathbb R} Z(c_1, \ldots, c_{n+d})\subset Q^q(\mathbb R^{n+d+1}). $$ We have already noted that the map $g_i : Z/\Sy_q\to\mathbb R^{n+d+1}$ taking any configuration to its $i$-th point w.r.t. the coordinate $x_{n+d+1}$ is a diffeomorphism. For any configuration $(p_1,\ldots, p_q)\in Z$ put $$ h(p_1,\ldots, p_q) = \sum_{i=1}^q g_i(p_1, \ldots, p_q), $$ i.e. the center point of the configuration. The map $h$ is smooth on $Z/\Sy_q$ and for small enough $\delta_i$ it is a diffeomorphism onto $\mathbb R^{n+d+1}$. Hence $h^{-1}(0)$ is the only configuration in $Q_0^q(\mathbb R^{n+d+1})$ that is mapped into single point by $f$. Since the configuration $h^{-1}(0)$ lies on a translate of the moment curve, which is a convex curve, then its points span some $q-1$-dimensional linear subspace $L\subset\mathbb R^{n+d+1}$. Now any linear space $V\in G_{n, d+1}$, that is supposed to have coincident $q$-tuples in the fiber $Q_0^q(V)$, must contain $L$. Moreover, it can be easily seen that the map $f$ is transversal to zero and the condition $V\supseteq L$ defines the Poincare dual to $s_{q, d}$ homology class. From the well-known description of the (dual) Stiefel-Whitney classes it follows that \begin{equation} s_{q, d} = w_{d+1}^{q-1}(\gamma^\perp) \end{equation} in the cohomology $H^*(G_{n, d+1}, Z_2)$. Now it suffices to note that this cohomology algebra has generators $w_1(\gamma), \ldots, w_n(\gamma)$ and relations \begin{equation} w_{d+2}(\gamma^\perp) = w_{d+3}(\gamma^\perp) = \dots = 0, \end{equation} hence (\ref{dual-sw-power}) holds over arbitrary space modulo higher Stiefel-Whitney classes of $\eta - \xi$, because the number $n$ can be taken arbitrarily large, and the relations in (\ref{grass-gen}) are the only essential relations.

nodes.statement:
Passing to the particular case $q=4$ note that $\Sy_4$ is the square group $D_8$, and its cohomology is multiplicatively generated by three elements $a, b, c$ such that $$ \dim a = \dim c = 1,\quad \dim b = 2, $$ and the relation $ac=0$. u) ) = \prod_{i=1}^
u (t_i^2 + (a+c)t_i+b)(t_i+c). $$ to find the leading characteristic class of coincident $4$-tuples in codimension $d$ we have to find the coefficient at $(bc)^{
